acceptance: The site-parity report shows 0 stale allowances on develop.
A decision is recorded on whether stale allowances fail the gate, and the gate or its docs match it.
context:
Seen in the site-parity job for #2669 (2026-10-05): 'summary: 0 missing path, 0 missing fragment, ... 36 stale allow'. The gate failure in that run was a separate docs-header focus bug, fixed in #2675.

Correction 2026-10-06: an earlier note on this item said production still rendered with Sphinx and blocked the item on astro-site-53-cutover. That was wrong; it relied on the cutover item's stale tracker status. Production is Astro (benchbox.dev/docs/ generated by Astro 7.3.5/Starlight; deploy/routes.yml renderer: auto from #2685; site-deploy run 37406123669 built every route with Astro from tag v0.4.2). The block and the need were removed. Note for the owner: astro-site-53-cutover is still open in the tracker although the cutover has shipped.

Owner widened the scope (2026-10-06): correct all stale entries and re-audit every link-check exemption. Audit on develop d076a974d with a full site-parity build and a Sphinx linkcheck run (143 working, 16 redirected, 0 broken):
- known-broken-links.json: 36 of 66 entries no longer broken in the Astro build; removed. 30 remain.
- docs/linkcheck_ignore.txt: 4 patterns matched no link (localhost, cloud2.influxdata.com, api.onehouse.ai, pypi.nvidia.com) and the BTS TranStats /ontime/ entry's stated 404 is gone; removed. Others kept: they cover hosts that reject or time out CI runners; benchbox.dev/results/compare?ids= is test-pinned and needed by a drafted blog post.
- expected-removals-*.json and allowed-differences.json: 110 patterns match nothing in the Sphinx-vs-Astro build diff but all match in the diff against the published Sphinx baseline, which is what they record; kept.
- release-known-broken/v0.4.1.json: applies only to a v0.4.1 redeploy; tag is immutable; kept.
- redirect-pages.json, added-paths.json, allowed-inventory-losses.json: every entry verified against the Astro build. Owner action outstanding: the 7 added-paths.json entries still say owner_approval "pending".

Closeout 2026-10-06:
- PR #2736 merged as 1773cc093 (2026-10-06T19:15:46Z): the prune above. After it, site_inventory.py check on the Astro inventory reports 0 broken internal links and 0 stale allowances (acceptance 1).
- Acceptance 2, owner decision 2026-10-06: stale known-broken entries FAIL the site-parity check only. PR #2739 merged as fb98592e9 (2026-10-06T20:26:15Z) adds site_inventory.py check --fail-on-stale, used by make site-parity-diff; the production deploy link check keeps only reporting stale entries; docs/operations/site-deploy.md states the rule. site-parity passed on #2739 with the flag active, confirming 0 stale entries on develop.
Required contexts core, docs, landing, explorer, results-data, tooling and oracle-review were SUCCESS on both PRs; #2736's oracle-review passed on a stand-in the agent posted at the owner's explicit instruction (provenance comment on the PR); #2739 needed none. Worktrees removed.
description: The site-parity report lists 36 "stale allowance" entries: links recorded as allowed breakage (missing paths on the blog index, missing fragments in several ADR, examples and API-reference pages) that are no longer broken. Stale entries hide nothing today, but they would silently re-allow those links if they broke again. Remove them from the allowed-differences inventory and decide whether a stale allowance should fail the gate instead of only being reported.
